title: I Am, You Are
label: ch:sein
canDo: I can say what someone is in German, using any of the six present forms of the verb for “to be” — and say that I am tired.

payoff.summary: sein is the one German verb whose forms cannot be guessed from its infinitive, so this chapter meets them one at a time — bin, bist, ist, sind, seid, sind — and only assembles the grid once every cell has had its own lesson. It closes with müde, the adjective that finishes ich bin, and a short exchange that runs on nothing but this verb.
payoff.note: Chapter 16 is generated from schema-v2 lessons, so the payoff is atom-scored. It claims every atom the chapter introduces, because the practice lesson is where the six forms are first allowed to appear together: the grid there is a recap of six lessons, not an introduction, which is the only condition under which a paradigm table may be printed at all.
